facts.value: Civil law is the legal system used in most countries around the world today.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: The primary authoritative sources are legislation, especially codifications in constitutions or statutes passed by government, and custom.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: An early example of codifications is the Babylonian Codex Hammurabi.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: Modern civil law systems essentially derive from legal codes issued by Byzantine Emperor Justinian I in the 6th century.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: Roman law in the days of the Roman Republic and Empire was heavily procedural and lacked a professional legal class.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: A lay magistrate, iudex, was chosen to adjudicate.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: Each case was to be decided afresh from the laws of the State.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: The Justinian Code codified and consolidated Roman law up until that point, becoming known as the Corpus Juris Civilis.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: The Justinian Code influenced Western European legal systems until it was rediscovered in the 11th century.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: In the 19th century, both France and Germany modernized their legal codes with the Code Civil and Bürgerliches Gesetzbuch respectively.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: These codes heavily influenced not only the law systems of the countries in continental Europe but also the Japanese and Korean legal traditions.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: A central doctrine in continental European legal thinking is the concept of a Rechtsstaat, meaning that everyone is subjected to the law, especially governments.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: Countries that have civil law systems range from Russia and Turkey to most of Central and Latin America.
